newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue powering on falling rates.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue powering on falling rates.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares powered ahead on Tuesday as buy-orders from domestic investors kept pressure on a market boosted by falling interest rates on the local money market.
The 57-stock industrial index gained 35.80 points to a new all time high of 8,744.45.
"The buy-pressure is such that the market is only going one way -- up. There are quite a number of players holding money from the money market," one broker said. "It's like Christmas was not around".
Short-term interest rates on the money market have fallen over 10 percentage points in the past year to around 18 percent and are forecast to slide further in 1997 in response to falling inflation.
Many industrial counters traded 10 cents up from previous levels, but the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's big gain was recorded by cigarette manufacturer, Rothmans, which surged 250 cents at 4,570.
Minings continued subdued on Christmas eve, with coal producer Wankie trading unchanged at 550. The secondary seven-share mining index put on 4.40 points to 1,066.34.
